videos.title: Jensen Huang’s 700,000% Return Magnifies Nvidia Succession Risks
videos.description:
The office of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang has an unusual setup: The chief executive officer sits at an enormous oval desk facing his lieutenants, with room for more employees in stadium seating behind them. The arrangement — created as part of Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California — is purpose-built to suit how Huang runs the company. Though it’s not uncommon to see cultlike tech CEOs who obsess over details, Huang is in a class of his own. He has led the business since its very beginning 33 years ago, the longest such run in Silicon Valley. And even as Nvidia grew into one of the world’s most powerful companies — with a stock return of more than 700,000% — there’s still no one designated to potentially replace him.  Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductor reporter discusses the latest.

videos.title: How NIL Deals Are Turning High-School Sports Into Big Business | WSJ
videos.description:
Amateur athletes’ ability to sign endorsement deals that monetize their name, image, and likeness has pumped billions of dollars into college sports. Now it’s coming for high school athletes. 

For some parents and coaches, NIL deals create welcome opportunities for students to offset the growing costs of elite youth sports. Others, especially in the six states that still restrict NIL activity before college, think allowing teenage athletes to cash in on their personal brands takes the increasing professionalization of amateur sports too far.

videos.title: The Truth About How Data Centers Use Water And Power To Keep Cool
videos.description:
U.S. voters passed 40 ballot measures putting limits on AI data centers this week, as huge 1GW AI data centers from OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Amazon, Google and more push up water and power bills and put a strain on local resources. One of the issues that continues to come up is water usage, which is needed to cool the GPUs inside data centers running AI workloads. Closed-loop liquid cooling keeps water use low inside many modern AI data centers, but external cooling is still needed to move heat outside of the buildings and that requires large amounts of power or water in hot climates. CNBC visited data centers and spoke to researchers to find out the truth about how data centers use water.

videos.title: Why The Measles Outbreak Signals A Bigger Problem In The U.S.
videos.description:
The U.S. is on track to lose its official measles-free elimination status, as cases have soared across the country. Health experts warn that this could be indicative of more problems to come. Vaccination rates for a variety of diseases – that have been largely pushed out of the U.S. – have been falling in recent years. Steeper declines could lead to millions of new cases in the coming years, according to scientific prediction models. Watch the video to learn about what this means for public health.

videos.description:
The Korea-World Bank Partnership Facility (KWPF), established in May 2013, brings together Korea’s Ministry of Economy and Finance and the World Bank to strengthen collaboration and advance shared development priorities. This year’s KWPF Global Forum explored the transformative potential of AI in education and skills, highlighting how AI, innovation, knowledge, and Korean expertise can help strengthen learning and prepare people for the jobs of the future.
